gaps.text: No teacher ADHD rating scales on file
gaps.why: The neuropsychologist specifically recommended collecting teacher ADHD rating scales before the psychiatry visit, and none are among the documents, leaving no cross-setting baseline for diagnosis or medication monitoring.

gaps.text: Anxiety and mood not yet assessed
gaps.why: Generalized anxiety disorder is listed only as rule-out, and the parent reports negative self-talk ('stupid at school') and social withdrawal, but no anxiety or depression screening results are on file.

gaps.text: IEP missing the neuropsych-recommended reduced-distraction testing setting and broader assistive technology
gaps.why: With Processing Speed at 79 (8th percentile) and Working Memory at 86 (18th percentile), the IEP includes extended time and a word processor but not the reduced-distraction setting or the broader writing assistive technology the evaluator recommended.

gaps.text: Movement breaks dropped from the 504 when the IEP replaced it
gaps.why: The 2024 504 provided movement breaks every 30 minutes, which do not appear in the current IEP, even though the English teacher reports Jordan frequently leaves his seat.

gaps.text: No medication history or original pediatric ADHD workup on file
gaps.why: The pediatrician's ADHD diagnosis is cited without a date, supporting rating scales or any record of prior medication trials, all of which are needed for the requested medication evaluation.

suggested_letter.why: A psychiatrist letter citing the ADHD diagnosis and the low processing speed and working memory scores could ask the IEP team to add the reduced-distraction testing setting, writing assistive technology and movement breaks that are missing from the current plan. The letter could also ask teachers to complete ADHD rating scales, which would support medication monitoring.
